title: aicw-world-championship
label: "The Demon" Kyle Bane
how: Won an eight-man ladder match to become the first-ever AICW World Champion; retained through Seasons Beatings/Violent Night's own fatal four-way and a deliberately ambiguous "Stroke of Midnight" defense at New Year's Rasslin Eve before losing the belt to "Hard Line" Byron Brady in a steel cage at New Year's Revolution.

title: aicw-world-championship
label: "Hard Line" Byron Brady
how: Won a steel cage match against Kyle Bane at New Year's Revolution. AICW's own "No Gimmicks Needed" stages a Bane-Brady rematch for the belt, but the surviving document is truncated before any result; the belt is with Bane again by the Tokyo Thunder Festival, with no served document showing how it changed hands.
note: See aicw-world-championship-r3's own note for the unattested transition back to Bane.

title: aicw-world-championship
label: The Saint
how: Won the belt from Kyle Bane on the Tokyo Thunder Festival's own second night; retained through a Monday Night War title defense against Legion and an unchallenged appearance at Survival of the Fittest before losing the belt back to "Hard Line" Byron Brady at Steel City Meltdown.

title: aicw-world-championship
label: "Hard Line" Byron Brady
how: Won the belt back from The Saint at Steel City Meltdown, the last title match in the surviving record.

title: aicw-world-championship
label: "The Demon" Kyle Bane

won.source: Not shown in any served document. Bane is billed the defending AICW World Heavyweight Champion entering the Tokyo Thunder Festival; the surviving record's own last look at the belt before that ("No Gimmicks Needed", itself undated and truncated before its own Bane-Brady rematch resolves) has Byron Brady still champion, so this reign's own start is a genuine gap.

how: Billed champion entering the Tokyo Thunder Festival; lost the belt to a masked debutant, The Saint, on the event's own second night, with Byron Brady's own disguised interference as "Legion" deciding the finish.

title: aicw-television-championship
label: "Swingin'" Chandler Stone
how: Won a seven-man "Run the Gauntlet" elimination series on Fright Night to become the first-ever AICW Television Champion. The belt is held by Elvis by Seasons Beatings/Violent Night, with no served document showing the change.

title: aicw-television-championship
label: "Pretty Boy" Troy Walcott
how: Won the belt from Stephon T. Davis at New Year's Revolution; still champion, unchallenged, on "No Gimmicks Needed" and billed defending a reign of "over two months" entering the Tokyo Thunder Festival, where "The Convict" Oswald Bates dethroned him on the event's own second night.

title: aicw-television-championship
label: "The Convict" Oswald Bates
how: Won the belt from Troy Walcott on the Tokyo Thunder Festival's own second night; successfully defended it against Damion Sikes at the following Monday Night War and was still billed champion, unchallenged, at Survival of the Fittest. By Steel City Meltdown the belt is held by Legion, via an off-page saga the show's own recap narrates rather than stages: a Gino Valentini win voided, the belt then awarded by Commissioner fiat.

title: aicw-television-championship
label: Zeek Monkey
how: Won a three-way, also involving Billy Kane, against defending champion Legion at Steel City Meltdown, the belt's own last recorded change in the surviving record.

title: aicw-television-championship
label: Elvis

won.source: Not shown in any served document; Elvis is billed champion by Seasons Beatings/Violent Night and again, unchallenged, at New Year's Rasslin Eve.

how: Billed champion by Seasons Beatings/Violent Night and again at New Year's Rasslin Eve; Stephon T. Davis is billed the defending champion by New Year's Revolution, with no served document showing either transition.
note: Two unattested gaps bracket this reign: how Elvis won the belt, and how it passed from Elvis to Stephon T. Davis.

title: aicw-television-championship
label: Stephon T. Davis

won.source: Not shown in any served document; billed the defending champion entering New Year's Revolution.

how: Billed the defending champion entering New Year's Revolution, where he lost the belt to "Pretty Boy" Troy Walcott.

title: aicw-television-championship
label: Legion

won.source: Not shown in any served document. Steel City Meltdown's own recap has Commissioner Argie Otero voiding a Gino Valentini win over Oswald Bates and awarding the belt to Legion by fiat instead — an off-page ruling, not a staged match.

how: Awarded the belt by Commissioner Argie Otero's own fiat, off-page, after voiding a Gino Valentini win over the previous champion; lost it to Zeek Monkey in a three-way, also involving Billy Kane, at Steel City Meltdown.

title: aicw-international-championship
label: "8-Ball" Vic Garibaldi
how: Won the "King of the Hill" battle royal at Apocalypse '97 to become the first-ever AICW International Champion; billed champion, unchallenged, through Seasons Beatings/Violent Night, New Year's Rasslin Eve, New Year's Revolution, and "No Gimmicks Needed." By the Tokyo Thunder Festival the belt is held by Mista Smith, with no served document showing the change.

title: aicw-international-championship
label: Gino "Knuckles" Valentini
how: Won the belt from Chris Del Rio at Steel City Meltdown, after first winning the right to challenge in a match against Alex Raptor earlier the same show — the belt's own last recorded change in the surviving record.

title: aicw-international-championship
label: Mista Smith

won.source: Not shown in any served document; billed champion entering the Tokyo Thunder Festival, where commentary recaps "that's how Mista Smith became champion" without ever narrating the win.

how: Billed champion entering the Tokyo Thunder Festival and retained there against Chris Del Rio by double count-out. By the following Monday Night War, Chris Del Rio is champion, billed as having won the belt "Saturday night" — a show outside the held record.
note: The Tokyo defense itself did not change the title (double count-out); the loss to Del Rio happened off-page, afterward.

title: aicw-international-championship
label: "The Ultimate Male" Chris Del Rio

won.source: Not shown in any served document; billed champion entering the 13 April 1998 Monday Night War as having won the belt from Mista Smith "Saturday night," a show outside the held record.

how: Billed champion entering the 13 April 1998 Monday Night War and again, unchallenged, at Survival of the Fittest; lost the belt to Gino Valentini at Steel City Meltdown.

title: aicw-world-tag-team-championship
label: The Nubian Warriors
how: Won a tag tournament final at Apocalypse '97 to become the first-ever AICW World Tag Team Champions; lost the belts to the Perfectly Perfect Duo in a triple threat, also involving Money and Power, at Seasons Beatings/Violent Night.

title: aicw-world-tag-team-championship
label: The Perfectly Perfect Duo
how: Won the belts from the Nubian Warriors in a triple threat, also involving Money and Power, at Seasons Beatings/Violent Night, and held them through the whole of the surviving record after — still champions, five months into the reign by the fed's own last-recorded show.

title: aicw-inoki-cup
label: "Big D" Devon Burke
how: Won the eight-man Inoki Cup tournament's own final over Rory Christianson on the Tokyo Thunder Festival's first night, and successfully defended the cup the following night against Vic Garibaldi; still champion at the fed's own last-recorded show.

title: aicw-north-american-tag-team-championship
label: The Asian Assassination Squad

won.source: Not shown in any served document; billed champions on AICW's own Survival of the Fittest, the belt's only appearance in the surviving record.

how: Billed AICW's own North American Tag Team Champions on Survival of the Fittest; no document shows the title won, defended, or lost.
